re_line: Coalition landslide ends Victorian Labor's 12-year rule · NZ deadlock hands Opportunity's Qiulae Wong the kingmaker role · Vanuatu-Australia Nakamal Agreement in force · US builds K211m of PNG defence works · Fiji rejects COP31 'failure' label
morning_memo: Victoria's election delivers a Coalition landslide ending Labor's twelve-year run, with Jess Wilson set to take office and Canberra reading the result for federal signal.
New Zealand's final count leaves Opportunity newcomer Qiulae Wong as kingmaker, forcing Christopher Luxon to reverse his repeated pre-election refusal to deal with the party.

The United States has K211.27 million of defence construction underway in Manus, Lae, and Port Moresby, ahead of a planned K2.25 billion fuel storage facility under the PNG Defense Cooperation Agreement.

top_stories.headline: Coalition ends Labor's 12-year rule in Victoria
top_stories.body: Victorian Labor has been defeated after twelve years in government, with the Coalition likely to form majority government in what the ABC calls potentially one of the most complex results in Australian political history. Bloomberg reports the Liberal-Nationals set to win in a Labor rout. Acting premier **Ben Carroll** conceded after 123 days in the job. More than 1,700 polling centres closed at 6pm AEDT, with full preference distributions in the 88 Legislative Assembly districts not expected until the second week of December.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "Seats to watch and what to expect as Victoria's votes come in" · also Bloomberg

top_stories.headline: Deadlocked NZ election leaves political newcomer as kingmaker
top_stories.body: New Zealand's final election count has produced a deadlock that leaves Opportunity's **Qiulae Wong**, a political novice, as the decider of the next government, the Washington Post and AP report. RNZ reports that National needs NZ First, ACT and Opportunity to govern, with weeks or potentially months of talks ahead. **Christopher Luxon**, who said repeatedly before the vote that he would not do a deal with Opportunity, is now seeking one, and has cautioned against rushing to an agreement that falls apart.
top_stories.src_line: per Washington Post: "Political novice turns kingmaker after New Zealand's deadlocked election" · also AP

top_stories.headline: US details K211 million of active defence builds in PNG
top_stories.body: Construction is underway on *K211.27 million* ($47 million) of US-funded defence infrastructure in Manus, Lae, and Port Moresby under the US-Papua New Guinea Defense Cooperation Agreement, the Post-Courier reports. The works pave the way for a planned large-scale fuel storage facility valued at roughly K2.25 billion ($500 million). The disclosure lands a week after **James Marape** reassured Beijing over PNG's pacts with Western partners.
top_stories.src_line: per PNG Post-Courier: "U.S. details K211.27M in active defense builds ahead of K2.25B fuel storage project"

top_stories.headline: Vanuatu-Australia Nakamal Agreement takes effect
top_stories.body: Vanuatu Prime Minister **Jotham Napat** and Australian Prime Minister **Anthony Albanese** announced the entry into force of the Vanuatu-Australia Nakamal Agreement, which the Vanuatu Daily Post calls historic. The agreement takes effect days after Vanuatu's coalition rejected a *$500 million* pact over a net zero clause, and in the same month Canberra concluded its treaty with Solomon Islands.
top_stories.src_line: per Vanuatu Daily Post: "Vanuatu–Australia Nakamal Agreement enters into force"

overnight_items.headline: Wong's foreign policy speech leaves silences on alliance management
overnight_items.body_text: Foreign Minister **Penny Wong** warned in a major speech this week that growing competition between the United States and China is making the world more dangerous, the ABC reports, but left what it calls notable silences on managing an ally whose president intervened in markets to add a trillion dollars to one company's value while announcing new tariffs mid-negotiation. Southeast Asian states are absorbing parallel shocks to data-centre investment and Nvidia chip access.

overnight_items.headline: ADF sexual violence inquiry opens Tuesday under Stott Despoja
overnight_items.body_text: Former senator **Natasha Stott Despoja** will lead a once-in-a-generation inquiry into sexual violence within the Australian Defence Force, opening Tuesday, with hearings from around mid-2027 and a report expected later that year. She said nothing is off the table, including technology-facilitated abuse such as the recording device found in the women's bathroom aboard HMAS Leeuwin in October. The inquiry was a recommendation of the Royal Commission into Defence and Veteran Suicide.

overnight_items.headline: PNG sells off power stations donated by Australia
overnight_items.body_text: Papua New Guinea has sold off power stations donated by Australia, the ABC reports. The buyer, sale price, and the government's rationale were not stated in the published summary. Australian-funded electrification has been a core plank of Canberra's PNG development programme alongside the US and Japanese partners in the PNG Electrification Partnership.

overnight_items.headline: Funding gaps threaten Fiji's El Niño drought response
overnight_items.body_text: Fiji's ability to respond to the worsening El Niño drought hinges on securing funding, Permanent Secretary for Environment and Climate Change **Sivendra Michael** said, with an inter-ministerial task force led by the National Disaster Risk Management Office reviewing capital funding inside operating budgets for money to reallocate. Fiji's first direct-access proposal, worth US$20 million, is intended for community relocation rather than drought relief. The Loss and Damage Fund board meets in December.

overnight_items.headline: Fiji logs 6.7 tonnes of meth and cocaine seized since 2021
overnight_items.body_text: Fiji recorded 52 narcotics seizures between 2021 and 2026, including 4,082 kilograms of methamphetamine and 2,652 kilograms of cocaine, Fiji Sun reports. Seventy-six cocaine packages washed ashore across outlying islands over the period. Eleven detections were offshore, with the United States the single largest origin, and consignments traced to the Netherlands, Canada, Belgium, France, Brazil, Mozambique, Malaysia, the United Kingdom, Malawi, India, and Nigeria.

overnight_items.headline: New regional technology association spans 22 Pacific states and territories
overnight_items.body_text: A new regional technology association has launched to connect 22 Pacific Island countries and territories and expand opportunities in artificial intelligence, digital innovation and technology development, the Post-Courier reports. Digital infrastructure and undersea cable financing have been among the most contested fields of donor competition in the region.

aukus_watch.headline: Report: Marles granted powers to override laws to aid the US
aukus_watch.body_text: Deputy Prime Minister **Richard Marles** has been given powers to override Australian laws in order to assist the United States, The Saturday Paper reports, with critics quoted describing an element of the government's account as a flat-out lie. The scope of the provisions was not detailed in the available summary. The report follows defence legislation that one independent MP last week called very rushed and an overreach.

aukus_watch.headline: Lowy: AUKUS risks repeating the mistake made of two sidelined 1930s officers
aukus_watch.body_text: Two officers sidelined in the 1930s were proved right about Australia's defence needs, the Lowy Interpreter argues, and AUKUS risks repeating that institutional failure to hear dissent on force structure. The piece lands alongside ASPI's running argument that the public case for Australian SSNs remains incomplete on deterrence and trade protection.

pacific_wire.headline: MPs who back Bougainville independence should resign, Namah says
pacific_wire.body_text: Vanimo-Green MP **Belden Namah** told Papua New Guinea's Parliament that members who vote in favour of Bougainville's political independence should resign, arguing MPs are bound by oaths taken under sections 6 and 249 of the Constitution. It was his fourth debate on the question.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji rejects the COP31 'failure' label
pacific_wire.body_text: Permanent Secretary **Sivendra Michael** said Fiji and other small island states refused a weak cover text at COP31 in Antalya because accepting a bad deal would have been the real failure. The cover decision was not adopted but *46 of 67* core agenda items were. Asked whether Australia, which led the negotiations, turned its back on the Pacific, he said no president can override a veto.

pacific_wire.headline: Rarotonga water authority warns on levels as El Niño dries catchments
pacific_wire.body_text: Rarotonga's water authority has warned of low levels and called for water subsidies as El Niño dries catchments, with the Cook Islands government still assessing the situation, Cook Islands News reports. Forecast models warn the event could rival or exceed previous El Niños, with drier conditions across much of the Southern Group and wetter conditions in parts of the Northern Group.

pacific_wire.headline: Samoa Observer reporter convicted of wilful trespass at PM's residence
pacific_wire.body_text: District Court Judge **Talasa Atoa Saaga** found Samoa Observer senior reporter **Sulamanaia Manaui Faulalo** guilty of wilful trespass at the residence of Prime Minister **La'aulialemalietoa Leuatea Schmidt**, in a case brought after a complaint by the prime minister's son. The judge said journalists have no unrestricted right to enter or remain on private property. Faulalo was charged on April 10 and pleaded not guilty.

pacific_wire.headline: Bainimarama loses pension appeal, ordered to pay $5,000 in costs
pacific_wire.body_text: A five-member Court of Appeal panel unanimously upheld the statutory formula used to calculate former prime minister **Voreqe Bainimarama**'s pension, rejecting his argument that more than ten years in office entitled him to 75 percent of his final salary. He must pay $5,000 in costs within 21 days.

pacific_wire.headline: Vanuatu court finds biofuel firm deceived Malekula landowner
pacific_wire.body_text: The Supreme Court of Vanuatu dismissed a claim by South Pacific Biofuels Limited against customary landowner **Gibeon Nathan** and his family over a disputed *1,128-hectare* lease at Espigels Bay on Malekula, finding the company had deceived Nathan. Customary land tenure disputes remain among the most sensitive areas of foreign investment in Vanuatu.

pacific_wire.headline: New Guinea Islands forum pushes regional autonomy as party launches in Kokopo
pacific_wire.body_text: A one-day forum on decentralisation and the local economy opened Saturday at the Gazelle International Hotel in Kokopo, drawing participants from the New Guinea Islands provinces, alongside the launch of a new political party. Autonomy demands from the provinces run in parallel with the Bougainville independence question now before Parliament.

pacific_wire.headline: Aneityum to offer Year 11 for the first time in 2027
pacific_wire.body_text: Students on Aneityum, Vanuatu's southernmost inhabited island, will be able to start Year 11 at home from 2027, with Teruja Junior Secondary School expanding into senior secondary education. Separately, Women Against Crime and Corruption chairwoman **Jenny Ligo** called on the government to replace tent classrooms with permanent buildings.

new_zealand.headline: National needs NZ First, ACT and Opportunity for a majority
new_zealand.body_text: National requires all three of NZ First, ACT and Opportunity to form a government, RNZ reports, with weeks or potentially months of negotiation ahead. **Christopher Luxon** cautioned against rushing to an agreement that falls apart. A four-party arrangement would be the widest coalition New Zealand has assembled under MMP.

new_zealand.headline: RNZ analysis: Luxon's Opportunity reversal weakens an already weak leader
new_zealand.body_text: Luxon said over and over that he would not do a deal with Opportunity, RNZ's analysis notes, and is now seeking one in a scenario it calls entirely predictable before the vote. The piece argues the reversal leaves a leader already weak in charge of a weakened caucus weaker still, with the final result forcing him either to accept the terms or walk away.

china_in_the_pacific.headline: Solomons pledges no foreign base and no militarised infrastructure
china_in_the_pacific.body_text: Solomon Islands has pledged to keep its critical infrastructure free from militarisation and unauthorised access, and never to allow a foreign military base on its soil, under its new agreement with Australia, the ABC reports. The pledge follows confirmation on November 27 that the country's security pact with China has lapsed.

canberra_politics.headline: Albanese rules out frontbench changes as polling sours
canberra_politics.body_text: **Anthony Albanese** said Friday he is not contemplating major changes to Labor's frontbench before the next election, after passing a slew of bills in parliament's final sitting days, Tom McIlroy writes. Two-thirds of voters believe the country is heading in the wrong direction, and Coalition MPs think their side is cutting through more effectively than the prime minister.

canberra_politics.headline: SMH: One Nation's Victorian showing is the federal variable to watch
canberra_politics.body_text: **Ben Carroll** has conceded defeat in Victoria, the SMH notes, with the federal consequence for Albanese resting on whether the result is irregular around the margins. The ABC reports the number of One Nation MPs in the next Victorian parliament, and their influence, remains unknown.

canberra_politics.headline: Hartcher: predictions of Albanese's defeat suffer from amnesia
canberra_politics.body_text: Peter Hartcher writes that current predictions about the next federal election could only come from people suffering profound amnesia, setting out the two conditions that would have to be met for **Anthony Albanese** to lose. Labor holds 94 of 150 seats, and the next election must be held on or before 20 May 2028.

canberra_politics.headline: AFR profiles Jess Wilson, 36, inheriting Victoria's finances
canberra_politics.body_text: **Jess Wilson**, 36, has gone from unlikely opposition leader to the woman who must pull Victoria out of an economic hole that has been deepening for years, the AFR writes. A first-term MP taking the premiership would be an unusual elevation in a state that is the largest subnational borrower in the Commonwealth.

canberra_politics.headline: NSW Labor members accuse leadership of preselection by captain's call
canberra_politics.body_text: Labor's New South Wales leadership has been accused of alienating members and undermining democratic process after multiple state election candidates were preselected by captain's call rather than rank and file ballot. Premier **Chris Minns** announced Friday that commercial litigator **Jade Tyrrell** will contest the marginal Liberal-held seat of Lane Cove in March.

canberra_politics.headline: Canberra Liberal MLA quits party for the crossbench
canberra_politics.body_text: **Peter Cain** will leave the Canberra Liberals to sit as an independent on the ACT Legislative Assembly crossbench, saying the move will let him hold the government to account more effectively. The departure follows a fortnight of defection pressure on the federal Coalition, including Nationals discussion of a $500,000 penalty for defectors.

business_economy.headline: Reserve Bank of Fiji reopens $100 million drought lending facility
business_economy.body_text: Businesses hit by the El Niño drought can borrow up to $200,000 at a maximum interest rate of 3.99 percent from December 1 under the reopened $100 million Disaster Rehabilitation and Containment Facility, Governor **Ariff Ali** said. The facility runs to April 30, 2027, with repayment terms up to five years, and follows the national state of disaster declared on November 18.

business_economy.headline: Fiji employers blame agents for 6,000 work permit rejections
business_economy.body_text: Fiji Commerce and Employers Federation chief executive **Edward Bernard** said recruitment agents are behind most of the fake documents that led to 6,000 work permit rejections between August 2024 and November 2025, and called on the immigration ministry to publish its certified agents. Foreign worker numbers grew *79 percent* between 2022 and 2025 against 10 percent for locals. Fiji holds labour agreements only with Australia and New Zealand.

business_economy.headline: Smallholders face $10,000 fines under Fiji's proposed Yaqona Bill
business_economy.body_text: The Social Empowerment Education Programme warned a parliamentary committee that smallholder yaqona farmers and roadside vendors could face fines up to $10,000 or two years' imprisonment under Clause 36 of the Yaqona (Kava) Bill 2026. The 2024 national census recorded 14,532 yaqona farming households, about 93 percent of which rely on the crop as their main income.

calendar_watch.event: Reserve Bank of Fiji drought lending facility opens to applicants
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Sets the terms on which Fijian firms can borrow through a drought the government has declared a national disaster.

calendar_watch.event: ADF sexual violence inquiry opens under Natasha Stott Despoja
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Begins the Royal Commission follow-on process that will shape Defence personnel policy into 2027.

calendar_watch.event: Loss and Damage Fund board meeting
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Determines whether Pacific states can draw on the fund as El Niño drought spreads across Fiji and the Cook Islands.

calendar_watch.event: Full preference distribution in Victoria's 88 Legislative Assembly districts
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Settles the size of the Coalition majority and One Nation's presence in the next Victorian parliament.
Labor's preselection disputes in marginal seats like Lane Cove set up its defence of government in the largest state.

key_stat.label: US defence construction underway in PNG
key_stat.context: Active US-funded builds in Manus, Lae, and Port Moresby precede a planned K2.25 billion fuel storage facility under the Defense Cooperation Agreement.

also_today.headline: The hidden strength keeping peace in the Pacific
also_today.body_text: **Grant Bayldon**, chief executive of World Vision Australia, argues that in Solomon Islands seawalls and water systems are not enough, and that trust, tradition and inclusion are what keep climate pressure from tipping into conflict.

also_today.headline: Taiwan votes in nine-in-one local elections
also_today.body_text: More than 11,000 local government positions are contested in Taiwan's nine-in-one elections, with results expected Saturday evening. Campaigns focused on housing, transport and jobs rather than cross-strait relations. Analysts say Beijing will watch closely, and Taiwan has warned of possible Chinese interference.

also_today.headline: Fiji launches six-month agripreneur programme for 70 young farmers
also_today.body_text: Seventy Fijians aged 18 to 35, with at least 40 percent female participation, will be trained to turn farming into profitable businesses under a new government-backed Youth Agripreneurs Success Pathway Programme run with the Ministry of Agriculture, Waterways and Environment.
